To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a sequence of bent crystals with a parallel orientation can be used as a primary halo collimator for a high energy accelerator, and that this collimation is more efficient than expected from independent reflections.
a sequence of bent crystals can deflect a high-energy proton beam by a large angle with the efficiency close to one.

the beam deflection in the crystal multi reflector with a large number of strips can be much larger than the estimation obtained by the sum of the deflections of the strips working independently, because the beam volume reflection in one of the crystal strips increases the probability of volume reflection of the particles in the subsequent ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physics of high-energy particle interactions with matter, with a particular focus on the physics of high intensity proton accelerators.
the physics and technology of high energy beam manipulation in the regime of multiple volume reflections in bent crystals.
the development of the crystal collimation technique, which is one of the key technologies of the high-intensity proton accelerator projects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multiple reflections of high-energy particles in bent crystals are not just a curiosity, but a very important and promising tool in high-energy physics.
the multiple volume reflections of high energy protons are a very efficient and reliable technique for beam collimation.
the volume reflection is a very efficient method of beam collimation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for efficient beam collimation in a sequence of parallel crystals, which is based on the volume capture and multiple volume reflections.
we have shown that the multiple reflections of high energy particles in a sequence of silicon crystals is a promising technique for the halo collimation of future high energy accelerators.
the volume capture is a powerful tool for the collimation of high energy beams.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the efficiency of a bent crystal reflector can be much higher than that of an independent reflection.
the efficiency of volume reflection in a bent crystal can be increased by using the sequence of bent crystals.
the efficiency of the bent crystal collimator is not limited to 1% as it was assumed in the literature.
